experiments.title: Typed events: the elegant type that slowed down every call site
experiments.question: Does a mapped type with an `as` clause, indexed at every call site, make type-checking measurably slower than inferring the event name from a generic parameter?
experiments.verdict: Yes. On an Apple M3 Pro (12 cores), inferring the event name from the generic parameter cut check time by 52% with TypeScript 6 and by 57% with TypeScript 7 (51% to 65% from the fastest and slowest runs); on a 1-core Intel Xeon, by 41% and 65%. The safety check passed on both machines, so the type safety is the same. Narrowing `include` to `src` also stopped TypeScript from reading a generated file the app never imports.
experiments.takeaway: A mapped type with an `as` clause is evaluated backwards at each indexed call site. If you can infer the key from a generic instead, the checker does far less work.
notes: Both machines use the earlier protocol: 3 runs per condition, no warm-up, runs in sequence. On the Apple M3 Pro, the runs of TypeScript 7 after the fix vary more than the others (0.117 s to 0.159 s, 15.2% coefficient of variation), hence the wider range on that figure.
The two machines differ by CPU as well as core count: compare the before and after conditions within a machine.

experiments.title: TypeScript 6 vs 7 on type-fest
experiments.question: How much faster does TypeScript 7 type-check a real, type-heavy library than TypeScript 6, and how much of the gain comes from the native compiler itself rather than parallel checking? What happens to memory on a heavy workload?
experiments.verdict: On an Apple M3 Pro (12 cores), TypeScript 7.0.2 checked the type-fest sources 3.5× faster than TypeScript 6.0.3 (0.484 s vs 1.67 s): 2.6× comes from the native compiler alone (single-threaded) and 1.3× from parallel checking. On the full suite with type tests, TypeScript 6 stops at Node.js's default heap limit (4.0 GiB); with a 16 GiB heap it finishes in 74.6 s, against 14.1 s for TypeScript 7 (5.3× faster), but TypeScript 7 peaks higher in memory (11.6 GiB RSS vs 10.4 GiB). Stays open until a second machine is measured with the same protocol.
experiments.takeaway: Most of the gain comes from the native compiler, so expect it even on small CI runners. The default mode does not use all available cores: on this 12-core machine, `--checkers 8` checked the sources in 0.377 s, 22% faster than the default mode (0.484 s), and `--checkers 4` took 0.475 s.
notes: Types and Instantiations differ between TypeScript 6 and 7 on identical code, so never compare these counters across compilers. TypeScript 7's counters also vary slightly from run to run on the full suite, single-threaded included; on the library sources they are identical across runs.

Memory is peak resident memory (RSS) from `/usr/bin/time -l`, field "maximum resident set size", of the largest process: the Node.js process for TypeScript 6, the native compiler for TypeScript 7 (its launcher replaces itself with the native binary). It is not the compiler's own "Memory used" line, which for TypeScript 6 is the V8 heap.
Out of memory means Node.js's default heap limit (4.0 GiB here), not the machine's RAM: TypeScript 6 aborted with "Reached heap limit" at 4.2 GiB RSS, and completed with `--max-old-space-size=16384`.
One library (type-fest at one commit), check time only: no emit, watch mode or editor latency.

The two machines differ by CPU as well as core count, so compare conditions within a machine; the comparison between machines is indicative only. On the 1-core Intel Xeon, parallel checking gives 1.0× (0.9× to 1.1×) and the native compiler 4.0×.

The Intel Xeon results use the earlier protocol: 3 runs, no warm-up, not interleaved, no RSS. The Apple M3 Pro results use a discarded warm-up per condition and interleaved runs, with other applications open (load average 3.0 to 5.0). The full-suite runs stay noisy: up to 6.7% coefficient of variation.

The checker series was measured with other applications open (load average 3.0 to 4.2), and in a separate series from the default mode: the comparison between `--checkers 8` and the default mode crosses two series.
